quizzes.title: How the Press Freedom Index Works
quizzes.passage: Press freedom refers to the ability of journalists to gather information and publish it without undue pressure. Conditions for this differ widely from one country to another, and the World Press Freedom Index compares them within a single framework. The index ranks countries and regions according to the level of freedom available to journalists. To reach this ranking, it evaluates several aspects of the media environment, including how varied the media are, how independent they remain, and how well the legal system supports them. A central tool in this work is a questionnaire that gathers information on the conditions in which reporters operate. The results are released in a published report that places each country on a list and allows readers to compare nations with one another. Because the report reflects conditions at the time of assessment, a country's position can change when its situation changes. A free press is also described as one that acts independently, promotes transparency and holds powerful people accountable. Journalism therefore has a role beyond the newsroom, since it can give a voice to those who lack institutional power and can highlight injustices that would otherwise go unseen. For this reason, the index serves as a measure of how well journalists are able to do their work.

questions.q: Which organisation publishes the World Press Freedom Index?
questions.explanation: The index is published by Reporters Without Borders (RSF), a non-profit organisation.

questions.q: On what scale is each country scored in the index?
questions.explanation: Each country receives a score from 0 (worst) to 100 (best).

questions.q: What is the stated aim of the World Press Freedom Index?
options: Safeguarding the right to freedom of information
Setting trade rules for media companies
questions.explanation: The index aims at safeguarding the right to freedom of information.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The index ranks countries and regions according to the level of freedom available to journalists.
Reason (R): The index is published by the Press Council of India.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The ranking statement is true, but the booklet names Reporters Without Borders, not the Press Council of India, as the publisher.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Press Freedom Questionnaire   ->   A. Covers five categories
II. Aim of the index   ->   B. Safeguarding the right to freedom of information
III. Publisher's legal type   ->   C. Non-profit organisation
IV. Publisher's headquarters   ->   D. Paris, France
questions.explanation: The questionnaire covers five categories, the aim is safeguarding freedom of information, the publisher is a non-profit, and its headquarters is in Paris.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the design of the index:
I. The index evaluates the safety of journalists among its criteria.
II. A higher score on the index indicates less freedom for the press.
III. The organisation behind the index has its headquarters in Paris.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement II is wrong because scores run from 0 (worst) to 100 (best), so a higher score means more freedom.

questions.q:
How many of the statements below are correct?
(i) The Press Freedom Questionnaire covers five categories.
(ii) The index has been published as an annual report since 1985.
(iii) Each country's score runs from 0 (worst) to 100 (best).
questions.explanation: Statements (i) and (iii) are correct, while (ii) is wrong because the annual report has been published since 2002.

questions.q: In which year was the organisation that publishes the index founded? (year)
questions.explanation: Reporters Without Borders was founded in 1985.

questions.q: In which city is the publisher of the index headquartered? (city)
questions.explanation: The publisher has its headquarters in Paris, France.

questions.q: Which edition of the index is the 2026 report? (ordinal number)
questions.explanation: The 2026 report is the 24th edition of the index.

questions.q: What is the highest score a country can receive in the index? (number)
questions.explanation: Scores run from 0 (worst) to 100 (best).

questions.q: From which year has the index been published as an annual report? (year)
questions.explanation: The index has been published annually since 2002.

questions.q: What type of organisation publishes the index? (one word)
questions.explanation: The index is published by a non-profit organisation.

questions.q: What right does the index aim to safeguard? (three words)
accept: the right to freedom of information
questions.explanation: The stated aim is safeguarding the right to freedom of information.

quizzes.title: Press Freedom: Challenges and Role
quizzes.passage: Press freedom is shaped by a number of pressures, and financial strain is among the most widely noted. Media outlets in many countries face financial instability, which can threaten independent and unbiased reporting. Freedom of expression is regarded as vital to preserve journalistic integrity and to prevent undue influence from state or private actors. A free press is described as one that acts independently, promotes transparency and holds powerful people accountable. Its work reaches beyond the newsroom, since it highlights systemic injustices and enables public participation in democratic discourse through information, critique and civic dialogue. News coverage can also influence discussions in parliamentary and legislative bodies. A widely quoted line makes a similar point in a few words: where the press is free, and every man able to read, all is safe. These roles explain why the press is treated as significant in public life. Taken together, the pressures on the press and the roles it plays help explain why its condition matters to a society as a whole. Independence, transparency and accountability are therefore the qualities by which such a press is described. Freedom of the press is linked to a range of functions, from informing the public to examining those in power.

questions.q: The press is often called the fourth pillar of democracy. Alongside which three organs is it counted?
questions.explanation: The booklet counts the press alongside the legislature, judiciary and executive.

questions.q: During the pandemic, the media acted as which of the following?
options: A source of advertising revenue for governments
A replacement for public health services
A critical communication tool between government and citizens
questions.explanation: During the pandemic, media was a critical communication tool between government and citizens.

questions.q: Whose remark on a free press and literacy is quoted in the booklet?
questions.explanation: The booklet quotes Thomas Jefferson's line that where the press is free and every man able to read, all is safe.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Freedom of the press in India is treated as part of freedom of speech and expression under the Constitution.
Reason (R): Article 19(2) of the Constitution lists reasonable restrictions on freedom of speech and expression.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but Article 19(2) describes restrictions rather than explaining why the press is part of free speech.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Article 19(2)   ->   A. Reasonable restrictions on the right
II. Romesh Thappar vs State of Madras (1950)   ->   B. Freedom of press lies at the foundation of democratic organisations
III. Press as voice of the voiceless   ->   C. Gives visibility to those without institutional power
IV. Press sparks public debate   ->   D. Precursor to legislative and social reform
questions.explanation: Article 19(2) allows reasonable restrictions, the Romesh Thappar case held the press is foundational, and the press gives visibility to the voiceless and sparks debate that leads to reform.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the press in India:
I. Freedom of media is an absolute freedom under the Constitution.
II. Community journalism is described as promoting social cohesion and local accountability.
III. Political instability is linked to a decline in media freedom.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement I is wrong because media freedom is not an absolute freedom, while II and III reflect the booklet.

questions.q:
How many of the statements below are correct?
(i) The press serves as a bridge between the governed and the governing.
(ii) Article 19(2) states that freedom of the press is absolute.
(iii) During the pandemic, media reduced panic and fought misinformation.
questions.explanation: Statements (i) and (iii) are correct, while (ii) is wrong because Article 19(2) allows reasonable restrictions.

questions.q: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution is freedom of the press treated as part of freedom of speech? (article number with sub-clause)
questions.explanation: Freedom of the press is treated as part of freedom of speech and expression under Article 19(1)(a).

questions.q: In 1950, which Supreme Court case said freedom of the press lies at the foundation of all democratic organisations? (first party's name)
accept: Romesh Thappar vs State of Madras
Romesh Thapar vs State of Madras
Romesh Thappar v State of Madras
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court made this observation in Romesh Thappar vs State of Madras.

questions.q: The press is called the fourth pillar of democracy, alongside the legislature, the judiciary and which other organ? (one word)
questions.explanation: The fourth pillar is counted alongside the legislature, judiciary and executive.

questions.q: During the pandemic, media acted as a critical communication tool between government and whom? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet describes media as a communication tool between government and citizens.

questions.q: Who is the author of the line 'Where the Press is Free, and Every Man able to Read, All is Safe'? (surname)
questions.explanation: The line is attributed to Thomas Jefferson in the booklet.

questions.q: Political instability is linked to a decline in what? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet links political instability to a decline in media freedom.

questions.q: Besides local accountability, what social value does community journalism promote? (two words)
questions.explanation: Community journalism promotes social cohesion, local accountability and political activism.
